function.name: uber_eat_order
function.description: Place an order for food delivery on Uber Eats by specifying the restaurant and the items with their respective quantities. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

restaurant.description: The name of the restaurant from which to order food.

items.description: A list of food item names selected for the order.

quantities.description: A list of quantities for each food item, corresponding by index to the items array.

message.content: I’m sorry, but I don’t have access to real‑time data. I can’t look up the current temperature in Moscow right now. If you’d like, I can explain how to find it using a weather website or app.

We don't have real-time data. We can either say we can't fetch real-time data or we can approximate. According to policy, we should not hallucinate. We can say we cannot provide real-time data. But maybe we can use a public API? There's no tool for weather. So we should respond that we cannot fetch real-time data. Alternatively, we could ask if they'd like us to approximate based on typical weather patterns. But better to say we cannot fetch real-time data.
